We have applied first template 324324, got two precursors: product1: "Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1" and "Nc1ccccc1N". That matches splitting the amide? Actually original had C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N, so template 324324 likely breaks amide to give carboxylic acid and aniline di-amine? It gave "Nc1ccccc1N" (para? Actually aniline with two amines? It's an aniline with two NH2? The SMILES "Nc1ccccc1N" is p-phenylenediamine? Actually it's aniline with two NH2 at positions 1 and? It's a benzene with two NH2 at positions 1 and? The SMILES "Nc1ccccc1N" is aniline with two NH2 at both ends (para?). Anyway.

Now second template 1914396 applied to the first precursor (the sulfonyl phenyl with carboxylic acid). It gave two precursors: "Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1" and "O=C(O)CC(=O)O". So it broke the double bond? Actually turned the /C=C/C(=O)O into C=O (aldehyde?) and gave a dicarboxylic acid? The second product is O=C(O)CC(=O)O (malonic acid). So we have now three precursors: the sulfonyl phenyl with aldehyde (C=O) attached, the malonic acid, and the diamine.

Now we need third template 733 to apply to something. Likely to the aldehyde to form the double bond? Or to combine malonic acid with something? Let's see what template 733 does. We need to apply to one of the current molecules to get further precursors. Probably apply to "Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1" to break the aldehyde to something like a vinyl? Or maybe to the malonic acid to get something else. Let's check if template 733 matches the aldehyde-containing molecule. Use check tool.
